meta.title: Tourists Keep Falling for These Vietnam Visa TRAPS! (2026 Warning)
meta.description:
Traveling to Vietnam in 2026? These Vietnam visa and immigration mistakes can ruin your trip before it even begins.

Every year, travelers make simple Vietnam visa mistakes that turn into airport nightmares, denied boarding, expensive fines, deportation risks, and even future entry problems. Some lose time and money because they trusted outdated visa advice, fake agents, or misunderstood Vietnam’s immigration rules.

In this video, Attorney Ken Duong breaks down the 9 biggest Vietnam visa and immigration mistakes tourists must avoid in 2026. From not checking your entry stamp and making e-visa name mistakes to forgetting the arrival card, carrying undeclared cash, slipping money into your passport, and abusing tourist visas, this guide explains what can seriously ruin your Vietnam trip before it even starts.

If you are planning to travel, live, work, invest, or bring family to Vietnam and you are unsure about the correct visa or immigration path, this video could save you thousands of dollars, major stress, and potentially getting banned from returning to Vietnam.

Watch until the end because some of the biggest visa mistakes happen AFTER tourists already arrive in Vietnam.

comments.author: @tonymcmenim
comments.text: He doesn't understand. The visa gains you entry only. The visa duration is how long you have to use it, to present yourself at a border for processing, that is all. Your length of stay is decided at the border by the officer. By default they can give you a length of time that is the same as the visa validity but not always and they don't have to. If you say you are just going for a wedding or do some shopping then they may just give you a week. 30 day visa but 7 day stay. So be aware that the visa period and length of stay are two entirely different things, as they are in all countries.
